what_it_does: This paper describes a specialized chip built in a 28-nanometer manufacturing process that solves Boolean satisfiability problems (K-SAT): deciding whether a complex logical puzzle has a valid solution or proving that no solution exists. The puzzle consists of clauses (AND/OR groups) that must all be simultaneously true. Previous chip-based solvers could only find solutions when they exist but couldn't prove when none exist; this design handles both cases completely. The chip uses arrays of fast memory (SRAM) with two parallel reasoning paths: one direction traces from clauses to variable assignments, and the other traces backward from assignments to clauses, filling in forced values. Incremental state tracking keeps the reasoning efficient as the solver explores different paths.
